en: The *Śatasahasra-mudrā-dhāraṇī-sūtra*, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śikṣānanda of Khotan during the Tang Dynasty.
Thus have I heard. At one time, the Buddha was staying on Vulture Peak Mountain in the city of Rājagṛha, together with...
Together with a great assembly of bhikṣus and immeasurable bodhisattvas, the World-Honored One then addressed the bhikṣus: "There is a dhāraṇī named 'Hundred Thousand Seals.
You should all receive and uphold it together."
When reciting this mantra,
one should first take refuge in the Buddha Golden Broad-Face Radiant Banner and Śākyamuni Buddha.
Then he spoke the root dhāraṇī, saying:
*Tadyathā* (1) *Oṃ* (2) *Bodhi bodhi bodhi bodhi* (3) *Sarvatathāgataguhyadhara* (4) *Dhara dhara* (5) *Hara hara* (6) *Prabhara*.
Rabrahāra (7) mahābodhicitta (8) julu julu (9) śatākṣimiśantridite (10) sarvatathāgatādhiṣṭhānābhiṣikte (11) guṇe guṇapate (12) buddhaguṇavaśe (13) svāhā.
13. *kṣi kṣi* 14. *gagaṇatari gagaṇatari* 15.
*sarvatathāgatātiṣṭhitānupasaṃtari* 16. *śama śama* 17.
*praśama praśama* 18. *sarvabhava-praśamani* (ten)
9. *Sarvabodhisattvānām* 20. *Hulu hulu bodhimārge* 21.
*Pratisthite sarvatathāgatapratīṣṭita-śuddhe svāhā* 22.
At that time, the World-Honored One...
Furthermore, for the sake of the great assembly, he spoke this heart-mantra:
Oṃ sarvatathāgatavaiśvāsakṛte śaye śaye svāhā. At that time, the World-Honored One...
Furthermore, he again proclaimed the mantra that accords with the mind, saying:
*Oṃ huru huru jayamukhe svāhā*. If there are bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, upāsikās, or other men and women of pure faith who are constructing a stūpa, [they should recite it].
If one writes these dharani phrases and places them within a stupa,
one will obtain the same supreme merit as that of constructing hundreds of thousands of stupas.
At that time, all the bhikṣus, devas, nāgas, and the entire assembly of the eight classes of beings [were present].
Having heard what the Buddha had spoken, they rejoiced and practiced accordingly.
*The Sūtra of the Hundred Thousand Seals Dhāraṇī*.
